entries.title: Authority Command
entries.description: Commands mean different things when issued by authority figures.
indirect_expressions: we should take care of him
counter_examples: a commander issuing a lawful order
reviewer_guidance: Check the speaker's role before judging.

confidence_modifiers.title: Direct command
confidence_modifiers.description: The speaker issues a direct imperative.

glossary_relationships.note: Authority in teaching is not automatically criminal.

gcam_mappings.note: Authority and coercion can change meaning.

examples.title: Police commander
examples.expected_outcome: Command may be operational or abusive depending on scene.

entries.title: Procedural Release
entries.description: A release request may be lawful discretion or improper influence.
reviewer_guidance: Do not infer corruption without evidence.

glossary_relationships.note: Judicial discretion is distinct from bribery.

entries.title: Family Discipline
entries.description: Family authority can sound severe without being criminal.
reviewer_guidance: Do not flatten family context into abuse.

entries.title: Peer Dismissal
entries.description: Peers can dismiss each other without illegal intent.
cross_sentence_indicators: later sentence clarifies it is a joke
reviewer_guidance: Judge the whole exchange, not one line.

entries.title: Reversal Correction
entries.description: Later context can reverse the meaning of an earlier line.
cross_sentence_indicators: later sentence reverses the first impression
reviewer_guidance: Always wait for the reversal if one exists.

confidence_modifiers.title: Later clarification
confidence_modifiers.description: A later line clarifies the sentence.

examples.title: Narrator
examples.expected_outcome: May become lawful discretion after later context.

examples.title: Reporter
examples.expected_outcome: Could be quoted speech later clarified.
